definition: Parsing a person’s image into semantic body parts — head, torso, limbs — used in virtual try-on and pose analysis.
details: Parsing a person’s image into semantic body parts — head, torso, limbs — used in virtual try-on and pose analysis.

explainer.lead: Human part segmentation parses a person's image into semantic body parts such as head, torso, and limbs. It matters as a building block for virtual try-on and pose analysis.

tiers.eli5: It colors in each part of a person in a photo, like labeling the head, arms, and legs separately.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it to isolate body regions before tasks like virtual clothing fitting or pose work. A pitfall is that loose clothing, occlusion, and unusual poses blur part boundaries.
tiers.paperLevel: Defined as parsing a person's image into semantic body parts, such as head, torso, and limbs; it is used in virtual try-on and pose analysis.

explainer.example: A try-on system segments a shopper's torso and limbs so a garment can be fitted to the right regions.
